facts.raw_span: 15-year history of Parkinson disease
Hoehn and Yahr score, 3
20-year history of sleep disturbance
worsening dream enactment behavior
episodes of dream enactment became progressively more violent
assault on his wife and self-injurious behaviors
Yelling occurred multiple times per night
Violent behaviors were reported every other night
Initial polysomnography demonstrated obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), with an Apnea Hypopnea Index score of 8.5
Emergency department neuroimaging was unremarkable
Repeat polysomnography demonstrated an Apnea Hypopnea Index score of 12.8
one severe episode resulted in a head laceration after striking the wall

concepts.preferred_label: Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder
support_spans: worsening dream enactment behavior
episodes of dream enactment became progressively more violent
assault on his wife and self-injurious behaviors
one severe episode resulted in a head laceration after striking the wall
concepts.why: The patient's worsening dream enactment behavior, violent episodes, and self-injurious behaviors during sleep are characteristic of Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder.

support_spans: Initial polysomnography demonstrated obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), with an Apnea Hypopnea Index score of 8.5
Repeat polysomnography demonstrated an Apnea Hypopnea Index score of 12.8
concepts.why: The patient's polysomnography results show an Apnea Hypopnea Index score consistent with Obstructive Sleep Apnea.

support_spans: 15-year history of Parkinson disease
Hoehn and Yahr score, 3
concepts.why: The patient has a 15-year history of Parkinson disease, which is a known risk factor for Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder.
It explains the head laceration after striking the wall during a sleep episode.

rationales.F01: Long history of Parkinson disease increases the likelihood of Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder and Parkinson Disease itself.
rationales.F04: Worsening dream enactment behavior is a key feature of Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder.
rationales.F06: Assault on his wife and self-injurious behaviors suggest violent outbursts, which can be seen in Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder and Traumatic Brain Injury.
rationales.F09: Obstructive sleep apnea diagnosis supports the presence of Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
rationales.F10: Unremarkable emergency department neuroimaging reduces the likelihood of Traumatic Brain Injury.
rationales.F12: Severe episode resulting in a head laceration increases the likelihood of Traumatic Brain Injury and Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder.
